name: phase_reconstruction_via_flat_autocorrelation

phase_0.boundary_condition: the Nyquist-Shannon sampling limit and the spectral support constraint

VINIT.justification: the state of the system before any signal acquisition or spectral definition occurs

TANCH.justification: the final bounded output that satisfies both spectral and spatial constraints

AFWD.justification: the forward mapping from the temporal domain to the frequency domain

AREV.justification: the mapping from frequency space back to the temporal domain

CLINK.justification: the sequential application of constraints to refine the phase estimate

IMSCRIB.justification: the identity operation that enforces the known modulus while preserving current phase

FSPLIT.justification: the separation of the autocorrelation function into its constituent phase and magnitude components

FFUSE.justification: the recombination of the power spectrum and phase to recover the original autocorrelation

EVALT.justification: the state where the error between the estimate and the measured magnitude falls below the threshold

EVALF.justification: the state where the algorithm fails to reduce the error metric

ENGAGR.justification: a state where the estimate satisfies the magnitude constraint but violates the support constraint simultaneously

IFIX.justification: the permanent fixation of the phase values into a non-volatile record

phase_3.void_description: a zero-filled complex array with no defined magnitude or phase
phase_3.true_description: a phase estimate that yields the correct measured magnitude upon transformation
phase_3.false_description: a phase estimate that produces a divergent or incorrect magnitude spectrum
phase_3.both_description: a superposition of multiple phase candidates that satisfy the magnitude but not the support

steps.domain_action: initialize the complex frequency plane with zero values
record the measured magnitude spectrum from the sensor
derive the autocorrelation function from the power spectrum
transform the initial guess into the frequency domain
apply the measured magnitude constraint to the current estimate
transform the constrained estimate back to the spatial domain
apply the finite support constraint to the spatial signal
branch the process to evaluate convergence against the error threshold
confirm the error is within the acceptable tolerance
merge the validated phase with the magnitude to finalize the signal
detect a local minimum or stagnation in the error reduction
apply a phase-wrap correction to escape the local minimum
return the corrected estimate to the primary iteration loop
repeat the projection cycle until the convergence state is reached
verify the final signal matches the original autocorrelation properties
commit the reconstructed phase and temporal signal to permanent storage
close the reconstruction session and output the recovered object

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the Fast Fourier Transform algorithm and its inverse
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: complex-valued buffer passing between spectral and spatial domains
phase_5.memory_mechanism: a double-buffered array storing current and previous phase estimates
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the iterative loop controller managing the projection count
phase_5.alfs_store: the measured power spectrum acting as the immutable reference

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational cycles and floating-point operations per iteration
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: an unknown phase distribution with high spectral uncertainty
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a deterministic phase map with minimized spectral error
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information gained in phase is balanced by the reduction in the search space volume
